---
title: "Section 1.4: Using Formulas in Excel"
---

We often collect and record data in units that are most convenient to us. However, these units may not always be the ones we need when performing calculations. For example, we may record the lengths of tortoises in inches but later need to convert these values to centimeters or meters. In instances such as this, we can write basic formulas to transform existing data.

### Creating Formulas

To create a basic formula (i.e., any mathematical/statistical calculations), we start the calculation with an `=` symbol. Note that the formula `=1+1` appears in two different places in your sheet: one in the cell where you input the formula, the other in the **Formula Bar.**

![](/figs/sec_0104_fig_1.png){width=90% fig-align="center"}

Press {{< kbd Enter >}} ({{< kbd return >}} in macOS) to perform the calculation. Note that cell `A1` gives the result of the calculation, but the Formula Bar still displays the original equation. 

![](/figs/sec_0104_fig_2.png){width=90% fig-align='center'}

Below is a list of arithmetic operations with corresponding symbols on your keyboard.

| Arithmetic Operation   | Key             |
|------------------------|-----------------|
| Addition (+)           | {{< kbd + >}}   |
| Subtraction (−)        | {{< kbd - >}}   |
| Multiplication (*)     | {{< kbd * >}}   |
| Division (/)           | {{< kbd / >}}   |
| Exponentiation (^)     | {{< kbd ^ >}}   |
| Parentheses ( )        | {{< kbd ( >}} {{< kbd ) >}}|
: {.striped .hover}

### Creating Formulas with Cells and Fast-Fill Down a Column

:::: example
## Example 1.4.1.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Question 

Consider the following table from Example 1.3.1. Suppose we wish to create a new column with the dogs’ weights in kilograms. How can we do this efficiently in Excel (i.e., without typing a separate formula for each dog)?

| Name     | Breed              | Weight (lbs) |
|----------|--------------------|--------------|
| Bella    | Labrador Retriever | 65           |
| Max      | German Shepherd    | 75           |
| Carter   | Mixed              | 68           |
| Daisy    | Beagle             | 22           |
| Lucy     | Mixed              | 40           |
| Rocky    | Bulldog            | 50           |
| Molly    | Beagle             | 20           |
| Buddy    | Siberian Husky     | 60           |
| Sadie    | Mixed              | 35           |
| Cooper   | Bulldog            | 48           |
: {.striped .hover}

## Answer

**Step 1.** Create a new column header, `weight_kg`, in cell `D1`.

![](/figs/sec_0104_gif_1.gif)

**Step 2.** Type the formula that converts Bella's weight from pounds (lbs) to kilograms (kg).[^1] Type the formula `=C2*0.453592` in cell `D2`. Here the formula takes the value from cell `C2` and multiplies it by 0.453592. 

**Step 3.** Press {{< kbd Enter >}}/{{< kbd Return >}} to display the calculated value in cell `D2`.

![](/figs/sec_0104_gif_2.gif)

**Step 4.** Hover your cursor over the green square in the bottom-right corner of cell D2. Your cursor should turn into a black `+` symbol. Then **_double-click_**. Excel will fast-fill the formula down the column.

![](/figs/sec_0104_gif_3.gif)
:::

## Example 1.4.2.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Question

Open the `penguins.csv` file in Excel. Insert a new column next to `bill_length_mm` and convert the bill length values from millimeters (mm) to inches (in). _Note:_ 1 mm is roughly equal to 0.03937 inches.

## Answer

**Step 1.** When opening a `.csv` file in Excel, you may be prompted with a warning message asking you to save the file in an Excel format. Click on `Save As...` and save the file as an Excel workbook. (I am saving this in the Week 2 folder, but it might be different for you.)

![](/figs/sec_0104_gif_4.gif)

**Step 2.** Adjust the column widths for columns `C`, `D`, `E`, and `F` so you can read the column headers in their entirety. Hold down {{< kbd Ctrl >}} (or {{< kbd Command >}} in macOs) and click on the columns. Then click on the `Format` command icon and select `AutoFit Column Width`.

![](/figs/sec_0104_gif_5.gif)

**Step 3.** Add a new empty column to the right of `bill_length_mm` column by first selecting column `D` (`bill_depth_mm`). Then right click (or click with two fingers) to bring up the context menu. Select `Insert` from the menu.

![](/figs/sec_0104_gif_6.gif)

**Step 4.** Name the new column `bill_length_in` in cell `D1`.

![](/figs/sec_0104_gif_7.gif)

**Step 5.** In cell `D2`, enter the formula `=C2*0.03937` to convert the bill length in `C2` from millimeters (mm) to inches (in). Then complete the calculation by pressing {{< kbd Enter >}}/{{< kbd Return >}}

![](/figs/sec_0104_gif_8.gif)

**Step 6.** Hover your cursor over the green square on the lower-right corner of cell `D2`. When the cursor turns into a black `+`, double click to fast-fill the formula down the column.

![](/figs/sec_0104_gif_9.gif)

:::
::::

[^1]: 1 lb is roughly equal to 0.453592 kg.
